bib.title: KnowAgent: Knowledge-Augmented Planning for LLM-Based Agents

legacy_report:
SOURCE: KnowAgent: Knowledge-Augmented Planning for LLM-Based Agents. Yuqi Zhu, Shuofei Qiao, Yixin Ou, Shumin Deng, Shiwei Lyu, Yue Shen, Lei Liang, Jinjie Gu, Huajun Chen, Ningyu Zhang (Zhejiang Univ / Ant Group). arXiv:2403.03101v3 (21 Feb 2025). The extraction shows no venue, so treat it as preprint, though the text mentions "anonymous reviewers".

COVERAGE: All 24 pages. About 69k of 78,206 chars read directly (main text, appendices A-D, tables 1-6, and the start of the prompts). I skipped the reference list and the prompt tables 7-13 (ALFWorld prompt text), which are prompt boilerplate. Figures 3 and 4 are plots whose values did not extract, so their trends come from the prose only.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: Planning hallucination is defined as generating unnecessary or conflicting action sequences that violate action rules or commonsense. KnowAgent counters it with an explicit action knowledge base: a set of actions plus allowed transitions (a graph) that is written into the prompt as text.
  number: none
  setup: HotpotQA (actions Retrieve, Search, Lookup, Finish) and ALFWorld. Trajectories use ReAct Thought/Action/Observation, extended with an ActionPath P at each step.
  quote: "attempting to look up information without performing a search operation" or "trying to pick an apple from a table without verifying the presence of both the table and the apple"
  where: p.2 (Intro)
- claim: Action rules constrain the model to legal next actions. For example, Search can be followed by Search, Retrieve, Lookup or Finish.
  number: none
  setup: HotpotQA graph.
  quote: "Search:(Search, Retrieve, Lookup, Finish). This rule indicates that Search can lead to multiple pathways"
  where: §3.2.1
- claim: Fine-tuned KnowAgent-13b beats ReAct prompting by a large margin on both benchmarks. It also beats GPT-4 ReAct on ALFWorld at 13b and 70b.
  number: HotpotQA avg F1 39.26 vs 24.17 (ReAct, Llama-2-13b). ALFWorld unseen 58.71 vs 9.70. GPT-4 ReAct ALFWorld: 43.57 seen, 38.81 unseen. KnowAgent-13b: 54.29 seen, 58.71 unseen. KnowAgent-70b: 77.14 seen, 78.36 unseen.
  setup: Llama-2-chat backbones, LoRA fine-tuning, 2 self-learning iterations. HotpotQA test is 100 questions at each of 3 difficulty levels, scored by F1. ALFWorld test is 140 seen and 134 unseen tasks, scored by success rate.
  quote: "the 13b model achieves a performance increase of ↑15.09% (average) and ↑49.01% (unseen) over ReAct on the two datasets." Also "our approach surpasses GPT-4's performance on ALFWorld with both the 13b and 70b models."
  where: Table 1, §4.2
  note: The "15.09%" and "49.01%" are percentage-point differences (39.26-24.17 and 58.71-9.70). They are not relative gains.
- claim: Action knowledge alone, with no fine-tuning, already lifts ReAct on ALFWorld.
  number: Seen 13.58 to 30.00 (+16.42). Unseen 9.70 to 38.06 (+28.36).
  setup: Llama-2-13b, KnowAgent* (action knowledge in the prompt, not fine-tuned) vs ReAct.
  quote: "KNOWAGENT * 30.00 ↑16.42 38.06↑28.36"
  where: Table 2
- claim: Planning-hallucination rates drop sharply with action knowledge.
  number: Invalid action 0.35% (KnowAgent) vs 2.08% (ReAct) vs 6.87% (Reflexion). Misordered 1.23% vs 3.54% vs 3.87%.
  setup: HotpotQA, Llama-2-13b. FireAct is omitted because it only uses Search and Finish.
  quote: "ReAct 2.08% 3.54% Reflexion 6.87% 3.87% KNOWAGENT 0.35% 1.23%"
  where: Table 3
  example: ReAct issued Lookup before any Search, which Figure 5 marks as invalid.
- claim: Self-synthesized, rule-filtered trajectories match or beat data from GPT-4 or GPT-3.5.
  number: Fewer than 300 self-synthesized correct trajectories per iteration, vs 500 GPT trajectories for FireAct and NAT. Llama-2-7b HotpotQA avg: KnowAgent 33.47, FireAct 32.13, NAT 30.33. Llama-2-70b HotpotQA avg: 48.14 vs FireAct 48.04.
  setup: HotpotQA training subset of 500 instances. ALFWorld uses 85 instances per task category. The margin at 70b is only 0.1.
  quote: "KNOWAGENT selectively fine-tunes on fewer than 300 self-synthesized correct trajectories per iteration."
  where: §4.2, Table 1, App. A
- claim: Knowledgeable self-learning filters and merges trajectories. It keeps only correct trajectories that obey the action rules, with no invalid or disordered actions. When trajectories from several iterations cover the same task, it keeps the shorter path. It iterates until the gain is small.
  number: The paper uses 2 iterations. Training hyperparameters: LoRA r=8, alpha=16, 5 epochs, lr 1e-4, max length 4096.
  setup: Algorithm 1. Ablations run up to iteration 4.
  quote: "removing any trajectories that do not align with the provided AKm, particularly those with invalid actions or disordered action sequences."
  where: §3.3, Algorithm 1, Table 5
- claim: The action knowledge base matters more as iterations increase, and gains rise from iteration 1 to 2. Gains continue to iteration 4 but shrink.
  number: none (the plot values did not extract)
  setup: Figure 3: Llama-2-7b, 13b and 70b on HotpotQA, with and without the action KB. Figure 4: Llama-2-7b, Llama-2-13b, Vicuna-7b and Mistral-7b.
  quote: "as the number of iterations increases, the performance gap between w/o action KB and w/ action KB becomes more significant"
  where: §4.3, Figs 3-4
- claim: GPT-4-distilled action knowledge is roughly as good as the manual version on ALFWorld, but much worse on HotpotQA.
  number: HotpotQA 7b: manual 33.47 vs distilled 25.22. 13b: 39.26 vs 25.72. ALFWorld 7b: 20.15 vs 18.66. 13b: 52.24 vs 51.49.
  setup: The same actions with different rules, distilled with gpt-4-0613. The authors say the distilled HotpotQA rules were more concise, with fewer cyclical actions.
  quote: "Manual stands for human-crafted knowledge and Distilled represents the distilled knowledge from GPT-4."
  where: Table 4. The text claims "little difference in effectiveness", which holds only for ALFWorld.
- claim: Training cost is comparable to FireAct, which needs GPT-4 data.
  number: KnowAgent about 20 hours per cycle, about 40 hours total. FireAct about 50 hours with about 710 GPT-4 trajectories. Both use 8x V100 32G.
  setup: Llama-2-7b on ALFWorld.
  quote: "KNOWAGENT mandates around 20 hours per cycle, totaling approximately 40 hours for training."
  where: §4.3 Efficiency Analysis
- claim: The method generalizes across backbones. It is also applied to Vicuna-7b, Mistral-7b, GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4, but those results appear only in Figure 4 (Vicuna and Mistral). The table only shows the GPT models under ReAct prompting.
  number: none
  setup: "differences in how models absorb structured knowledge"
  where: §4.3

LIMITS
- Authors concede three limits. Only two tasks were tested, commonsense multi-hop QA and a household environment. Only single agents were tested, with no multi-agent systems. Building the action KB is still manual and labor-intensive, and GPT-4 distillation still needs manual adjustment.
- Error analysis: it struggles with complex queries and long-text summarization. Two HotpotQA error types are Inconsistency and Summarization errors.
- App. C: at 13b, FireAct is better on easy tasks. At 70b, KnowAgent's edge fades on Hard questions (37.76 vs FireAct 44.60) because its long prompt hurts long contexts.
- The 70b gain over FireAct is tiny (48.14 vs 48.04). Single runs and small test sets (100 per level) with no variance or significance tests are reported. This is my observation, since the paper reports no variance.
- The GPT-4 ReAct baseline is prompted, not fine-tuned. Llama-2 is dated, so the results may not hold on current models.
- The "knowledge" here is a hand-written transition graph over a small action set (4 in HotpotQA). It is not external factual knowledge.

BUILDS ON
ReAct (Yao et al., 2023b) for the trajectory format. CoT (Wei et al., 2022). Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023). FireAct (Chen et al., 2023a) and NAT (Wang et al., 2024) as fine-tuning baselines. BOLAA (Liu et al., 2023b) for the HotpotQA test set and the F1 reward. HotpotQA (Yang et al., 2018) and ALFWorld (Shridhar et al., 2021). Related work: AMOR (Guan et al., 2024), an agent framework built on a finite state machine, and Formal-LLM (Li et al., 2024c). Self-improvement work (Jiang et al. 2023b, Dou et al. 2024, Yang et al. 2024b). Vicuna and FastChat (Zheng et al., 2023), DeepSpeed, and Alpaca-style templating (Taori et al., 2023).

CODE: no code. Prompt skeleton (Figure 6, p.~7) for HotpotQA: "Start:(Search, Retrieve) / Retrieve:(Retrieve, Search, Lookup, Finish) / Search:(Search, Retrieve, Lookup, Finish)". The path trace format is "ActionPath 3: Start->Search[X]->Search[Y]". The prompt has four sections: Overview of Action Knowledge, Definition of Each Action Step, Principle of Planning Path Generation, Demonstrations.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.1): overview of an action knowledge base guiding planning.
- Fig 2 (p.3): the framework, covering action knowledge to text, path generation, and knowledgeable self-learning. This is the best single explainer.
- Fig 5 (p.8): the same HotpotQA question. ReAct does Lookup before Search and fails. KnowAgent follows Search to Search to Finish and succeeds. This is a good concrete example of planning hallucination.
- Fig 6 (p.17): the prompt layout and the graph.
- Figs 3 and 4: ablation curves (action KB, iterations).

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Text extraction is clean except that the figure text loses spaces. Plot data in Figs 3-4 did not extract, so no values are reported from them. I did not run the figures.py captions script. The ALFWorld prompt tables 8-13 were skipped. The author names were taken from the header.
